speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To understand the onset and progression of these symptoms, could you tell me when they started and if anyone else around you is currently sick?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola).

The classic progression of fever, rhinorrhea, headache, followed by a maculopapular rash that starts on the face and spreads downward while sparing the perioral area is highly characteristic. Given the patient's age and the specific timeline of symptoms, do you have access to the results of a serum IgM test for measles or a throat swab for confirmation? REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgM_Measles
